record_type_quote:
In contrast to claims of holistic processing, upright aligned composite face
         morphs were recently shown to be processed in the same manner as inverted
         or misaligned composite face morphs Cheng, McCarthy, Wang, Palmeri,
         and Little (2018). In the present paper, we replicate that work, using a set
         of schematic faces, which vary second-order features (e.g., lip height and
         eye separation) in the top and bottom-halves of the schematic face.

targets.authors: Cheng, X. J., McCarthy, C. J., Wang, T. S., Palmeri, T. J., & Little, D. R.
targets.title: Composite faces are not (necessarily) processed coactively: A test using systems factorial technology and logical-rule models.
targets.evidence_quote:
In contrast to claims of holistic processing, upright aligned composite face
         morphs were recently shown to be processed in the same manner as inverted
         or misaligned composite face morphs Cheng, McCarthy, Wang, Palmeri,
         and Little (2018). In the present paper, we replicate that work, using a set
         of schematic faces, which vary second-order features (e.g., lip height and
         eye separation) in the top and bottom-halves of the schematic face.
targets.outcome_quote:
Overall, performance in the composite face task is dampened by inverting the faces
and by misaligning the face halves. While the results are mostly in line with the composite
face task results reported in Cheng et al. (2018), there are some key differences between the
experiments. In that paper, they found the hallmark of holistic processing with both upright
and inverted faces whereas with the schematic composite faces, we found a hallmark for
holistic processing only in the upright and not the inverted face conditions.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Experiment 2 agrees with analytic processing in Cheng et al.; Experiment 1 explicitly contrasts its absence of the inverted-face holistic hallmark with the original. No overall verdict outweighs this stated contrast, so aggregate across both experiments as mixed.

targets.title: Information-processing alternatives to holistic perception: identifying the mechanisms of secondary-level holism within a categorization paradigm.
targets.evidence_quote:
To further investigate the difference in these findings, we extend our investigation
of face processing to schematic faces similar to Fifić and Townsend’s (2010) using the
paradigm developed in Cheng et al. (2018). Unlike the morphed faces in Cheng et al.
(2018) in which the category of the face depended on the observer’s perception of the
similarity between faces, the schematic faces are made up of fixed values that represent the
differences between the space between the eyes and the space between the nose and the
lips. We again employ SFT in order to determine whether there is any evidence for holistic
processing.
targets.outcome_quote:
Importantly, while the faces we used appear to be processed holistically in the stan-
dard composite task, there is no consistent evidence for coactivity when participants cate-
gorize upright aligned faces. We also did not find that upright faces are treated differently
from misaligned or inverted faces. Based on our non-parametric and parametric results, we
can also see that the main differences between the face conditions were quantitative rather
than qualitative (see Richler, Wong, & Gauthier, 2011)).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The paper explicitly investigates the discrepancy between Fific and Townsend’s coactivity finding and Cheng et al. using schematic faces, with a stated prediction about reproducing the former. Experiment 2 finds no consistent coactivity, contrary to that target finding. This is a retest by relationship, despite design changes; not merely a stimulus-source citation.

reasoning: Full 51-page preprint verified by title and Cheng/Little authors, includes both empirical experiments and complete references. New participant data re-test Cheng et al. (2018) and the conflicting schematic-face coactivity finding of Fific and Townsend (2010). Other methodological and general holistic-processing citations are not independent targets. Experiment 1 is a stimulus-validation task but its explicit original-result contrast must be retained in the Cheng aggregate.
